page: Microsoft Azure F4als_v6 is a compute-focused virtual machine from the Falsv6 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs with a single thread per core configuration. It runs at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Text processing performance is also strong. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls into the average range. Memory performance presents a clear tradeoff: while cached small-block read bandwidth and large-block write bandwidth are average, uncached large-block read bandwidth and the Passmark memory score are weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

Given the high-frequency CPU and low memory density, the F4als_v6 is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. It is well-suited for workloads such as web serving, single-threaded applications, text processing, and light software compilation. However, the low memory capacity and weak uncached memory bandwidth make it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale language model inference.
